traditions.name: Friday Night Planetarium Show
traditions.description: The Wayne State Planetarium in Old Main puts on free public shows most Friday evenings, with a tour of the current night sky and a fulldome film. Arrive early, since seats are first come, first served.

traditions.name: Old Main's Peregrine Falcons
traditions.description: Peregrine falcons live on a balcony of Old Main's clock tower, and the university calls them its winged Warriors. Look up at the tower to spot them.

traditions.name: Campus ArtWalk
traditions.description: Around 30 donated outdoor sculptures make the campus an open-air gallery you can visit any time. Start at "City with Halo" in front of the Thompson Home and follow the ArtWalk map.

traditions.name: Homecoming Game at Tom Adams Field
traditions.description: Homecoming week ends with Warrior football at Tom Adams Field, and fans are asked to wear green and gold. Join the crowd and cheer on the Warriors.

details.airportInfo: Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport in Romulus, southwest of Detroit, is Michigan's busiest airport and the main gateway to the city.
details.funFact: Old Main, the clock-towered heart of campus, was built in the 1890s as Detroit's Central High School. College classes that started there grew into Wayne State University.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are green and gold, and the teams are the Warriors.
details.transportationFact: The main campus in Midtown is easy to walk. The QLINE streetcar runs along Woodward Avenue at the campus's east edge and links it with Downtown Detroit and New Center.

buildings.name: Old Main
buildings.description: Malcomson & Higginbotham designed this brick and limestone landmark as Detroit's Central High School, which began classes here in 1896. Its clock tower still marks the corner of Cass and Warren.

buildings.name: McGregor Memorial Conference Center
buildings.description: Minoru Yamasaki's travertine-clad pavilion, completed in 1958, sits beside a reflecting pool and sunken garden under a skylit hall. It is a National Historic Landmark for its architecture.

buildings.name: Maccabees Building
buildings.description: Albert Kahn designed this 15-story Art Deco tower on Woodward Avenue, finished in 1927. Also called Wayne Tower, it is now owned by Wayne State.

buildings.name: Charles Lang Freer House
buildings.description: Wilson Eyre designed this Shingle-style house in 1892 for art collector Charles Lang Freer, whose gift founded the Smithsonian's Freer Gallery of Art. It now houses Wayne State's Merrill Palmer Skillman Institute.

buildings.name: Hilberry Theatre
buildings.description: Built in 1917 as the First Church of Christ, Scientist, this Neoclassical building became Wayne State's graduate theatre in 1963. It is being renovated as the Gretchen C. Valade Jazz Center.

buildings.name: Hilberry Gateway
buildings.description: This performing arts center opened in April 2023 next to the old Hilberry Theatre. Its 550-seat proscenium theater is home to the university's theatre and dance productions.

buildings.name: Walter P. Reuther Library
buildings.description: O'Dell, Hewlett and Luckenbach designed this home for the largest labor archives in North America, completed in 1975. It is named for UAW president Walter Reuther.

buildings.name: David Adamany Undergraduate Library
buildings.description: Built in 1997 at the center of Gullen Mall, this is one of Wayne State's largest libraries, with more than 2,000 seats. It is named for the university's eighth president, David Adamany.

traditions.name: The Bronco Statue
traditions.description: A 1,800-pound bronze bronco by sculptor Veryl Goodnight has stood on campus since 1997. It was first part of her larger work "The Day the Wall Came Down." Snap a photo with it.

traditions.name: Homecoming at Waldo Stadium
traditions.description: Each October WMU paints the town brown and gold for Homecoming, ending with Broncos football at Waldo Stadium. Join the crowd in the stands.

traditions.name: National Champions at Lawson Arena
traditions.description: The Broncos won their first men's ice hockey national championship in 2025. Catch a game at Lawson Arena and look for the championship banner.

traditions.name: Up Prospect Hill to Heritage Hall
traditions.description: WMU began on Prospect Hill, where East Hall opened in 1905 and a trolley once carried people up the slope. Walk up to Heritage Hall, the restored East Hall, and the North Hall portico beside it.

details.airportInfo: Kalamazoo/Battle Creek International Airport, southeast of downtown Kalamazoo, is the nearest airport with airline service.
details.funFact: Hyames Field, WMU's baseball park on East Campus, hosted the very first College World Series in 1947 and again in 1948.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are brown and gold, and the teams are the Broncos.
details.transportationFact: Kalamazoo's Metro buses serve Western Michigan University as well as the city and its suburbs.

buildings.name: Heritage Hall (East Hall)
buildings.description: East Hall, the first building of the Western State Normal School, opened on Prospect Hill in 1905. After its wings came down in 2013, the original core reopened in 2015 as Heritage Hall, home of the WMU Alumni Center.

buildings.name: Miller Auditorium
buildings.description: Opened in 1968 and named for WMU's third president, James W. Miller, this 3,497-seat hall is the fifth-largest auditorium in Michigan. Touring Broadway shows and the Kalamazoo Symphony Orchestra perform here.

buildings.name: Richmond Center for Visual Arts
buildings.description: Opened in 2007, this arts center houses part of the Frostic School of Art. Its first floor holds three galleries for rotating shows, the university art collection and student work.

buildings.name: Waldo Stadium
buildings.description: Broncos football has played on this East Campus site since 1914, and the full stadium opened in 1939. It is named for Dwight B. Waldo, the school's first president, and seats 30,200.

buildings.name: Hyames Field
buildings.description: Built in 1939 alongside Waldo Stadium, this baseball park hosted the first College World Series in 1947 and the second in 1948. It is home to Broncos baseball.

buildings.name: University Arena (Read Fieldhouse)
buildings.description: Read Fieldhouse opened in 1957 and is named for longtime basketball coach Buck Read. A 1994 renovation turned the floor 90 degrees and created the 5,421-seat University Arena.

buildings.name: Lawson Arena
buildings.description: This horseshoe-shaped, 3,667-seat ice arena opened in 1974 for Broncos hockey. Its old-style design and loud fans make it one of the toughest rinks for visiting teams.

buildings.name: John E. Fetzer Center
buildings.description: Opened in 1983, this conference center is named for radio pioneer and Detroit Tigers owner John Fetzer. Its lounge has an exhibit on his life.

traditions.name: Little Mac Bridge and the Ravines
traditions.description: Students voted the ravines and the Little Mac Bridge the most beautiful spot on campus. Cross the footbridge and look down at the stream below.

traditions.name: Carillon Music at Cook Tower
traditions.description: Every week the university carillonist plays music, from Bach to pop songs, on the bells of the Cook Carillon Tower. If you hear bells, someone is up there playing live.

traditions.name: Zumberge Pond
traditions.description: Lakers love to study, eat or just relax on the steps beside Zumberge Pond in any season. Take a seat and enjoy the view.

traditions.name: View from the Library Roof
traditions.description: The roof of the Mary Idema Pew Library gives a sweeping view of the Allendale campus, a student favorite when the leaves change in fall. Go up and take in the view.

traditions.name: Laker Football at Lubbers Stadium
traditions.description: Lubbers Stadium officially seats 10,444 but often holds thousands more fans, with a record crowd of 17,007 in 2021. Join them for a Lakers home game.

details.airportInfo: Gerald R. Ford International Airport, southeast of Grand Rapids, is the nearest airport with airline service.
details.funFact: Grand Valley is one of only three institutions in the Western Hemisphere with more than one carillon tower: the Cook Carillon in Allendale and the Beckering Family Carillon in Grand Rapids.
details.languageInfo: The school colors are blue, black and white, and the teams are the Lakers.
details.transportationFact: The Laker Line bus, run by The Rapid, links the Allendale campus with GVSU's campuses in downtown Grand Rapids along Lake Michigan Drive, and it is open to the public.

buildings.name: Cook Carillon Tower
buildings.description: This 10-story brick and stone clock tower, finished in 1994, is the focal point of the Allendale campus. Its 48 bronze bells were cast by the Royal Eijsbouts foundry in the Netherlands.

buildings.name: Kirkhof Center
buildings.description: Dedicated in 1974 as the Campus Center, the student union was renamed for Russel H. Kirkhof in 1984. It holds dining, meeting rooms and student offices, and the Laker Line bus stops outside.

buildings.name: Mary Idema Pew Library
buildings.description: SHW Group designed this library, which opened in June 2013 as the intellectual heart of the Allendale campus. It was the first library in Michigan to earn LEED Platinum certification.

buildings.name: Lubbers Stadium
buildings.description: Opened in 1973 as Lakers Stadium and later named for president Arend Lubbers, this is the home of Grand Valley football. It seats 10,444 and drew a record 17,007 fans in 2021.

buildings.name: GVSU Fieldhouse Arena
buildings.description: Opened in 1982 after the roof of the old "Dome" was condemned, this 4,200-seat arena is home to Lakers basketball and volleyball. It also hosts commencement and concerts.
buildings.address: Grand Valley State University, Allendale, MI 49401
